bird-recognition-analysis 1.0.13 changelog

- Updated documentation (SKILL.md): version, descriptions, and references.
- Removed the obsolete file: skill-card.md.
- Internal scripts (config.py, dao.py, util.py) updated; details not specified.
- General improvements to structure and maintenance.

- Updated user privacy and identity handling: all identity parameters are now managed internally, removing the need for user-supplied open-id.
- Streamlined SKILL.md documentation for clarity, including clear workflow, parameter instructions, and automatic report association.
- Strengthened data security and privacy by enforcing internal-only identity use—user identity is never shown, asked, or required as input.
- Refined history report query: all queries now mandatorily go through the cloud API, strictly forbidding local or memory-based lookups.
- Minor script and configuration adjustments reflecting new workflow (user identity auto-handled, simplified CLI usage and documentation).
- Removed deprecated files and updated resource indexing to match the new process.

- Major update to open-id acquisition and privacy policy: open-id must now be provided by the user and cannot be read from local config files.
- Updated privacy and data security statement: task-related files are transferred via HTTPS/TLS and not persisted on the server after analysis.
- SKILL.md clarified and streamlined regarding open-id usage and removed references to reading config.yaml or deriving open-id automatically.
- License added (MIT-0).
- Deprecated and removed redundant documentation file skill-card.md.

- Separated bird recognition logic into new module directory skills/smyx_analysis (added new scripts, config, and requirements files).
- Removed face_analysis module and all related files.
- Updated main scripts and shared utilities to support new structure under smyx_analysis.
- Adjusted documentation and configuration handling for modular skill expansion.
- No changes made to user-facing API or usage flows.

- Refactored internal imports and code structure in scripts/smyx_common for better modularity.
- Improved configuration management by updating config.py to handle config retrieval more robustly.
- Applied minor cleanups to util.py and __init__.py to standardize utility functions.
- Documentation unchanged except for typo fix in description. No workflow or feature changes to end user.

Changelog for version 1.0.6:

- Added or updated the version field in SKILL.md for clear version identification.

No changes detected in this version.

- Version number updated with no modifications to files or documentation.  
- All skill features, usage, and documentation remain unchanged.

- Major refactor and simplification of codebase: removed 14 files, including nested package structure under skills/smyx_common/smyx_common/.
- Updated and streamlined project structure; LICENSE.txt files added to main directories.
- Core scripts and configuration files revised to remove redundant layers.
- SKILL.md updated; now includes explicit version field and simplified structure.

- Introduced a common module ("smyx_common") for shared configuration, code, and utilities, with new Python package files.
- Added shared configuration files (config-dev.yaml, config-test.yaml, config-prod.yaml, config.yaml) under smyx_common to streamline settings management.
- Reorganized scripts and supporting modules to leverage the new common codebase and avoid duplication across skills.
- Updated and unified config.py scripts for both bird recognition and shared usage.
- No changes to main recognition functionality; primary update is internal structure and shared resource management.

- Initial release of the Bird Recognition Analysis skill.
- Identifies over 500 bird species in images or videos, distinguishing between similar species and subspecies.
- Supports custom model training for region- or species-specific optimization.
- Designed for ecological observation, wildlife monitoring, and home garden birdwatching scenarios.
- Strict rules for open-id acquisition and mandatory cloud-based report retrieval.
- Provides structured, Markdown-formatted historical analysis reports with clickable links to full results.
